say: One check failed and four ask to be read: the methods name the wrong correction family; everything else holds.

sections.title: The right data went in
sections.say: Were the recordings, rats, days and wires the ones the plan names?

checks.title: Every rat-day the plan names was read
checks.how: The rat-days in tab 11's results were matched against the plan's list of rats and the two sessions, Precon1 and Precon4.
checks.result: 16 of 16 rat-days (8 rats, Precon1 and Precon4) were read; none missing, none twice.

checks.title: The recordings are the originals
checks.how: Each recording folder's files were counted and sized and compared with the copy on the VACC.
checks.result: 2 of 2 recordings match the VACC copy file for file (33 and 35 files).

checks.title: J3 and J4 share a reference signal
checks.how: The zero-lag correlation between every pair of wires was measured on each rat-day, wire minus wire as well as raw.
checks.result: J3 on both days and J4 on Precon1 carry one signal on every wire (median r 0.71 and 0.64); the sets without them were worked out too.
detail: J3 Precon1: 0.72 raw, 0.08 wire minus wire.
J3 Precon4: 0.70 raw, 0.07 wire minus wire.
J4 Precon1: 0.64 raw, 0.11 wire minus wire.

checks.title: Wires used in each region
checks.how: Read from the electrode map and tab 8's choice of wires.
checks.result: Each region is the mean of its two sides; 3 wires were left out for clipping.

sections.title: The right logic was applied
sections.say: Do the numbers come out the same when worked out a second, independent way?

checks.title: Coherence worked out again by hand matches tab 11
checks.how: For one rat-day, coherence was recomputed with scipy straight from the recording and compared with tab 11's value for every pair.

checks.title: Every model clusters by rat
checks.how: Each GEE's groups were read back from its fitted model.
checks.result: 58 of 58 models have 8 clusters (5 to 7 for pairs with PER or RSC), exchangeable working correlation.

sections.title: The words match the numbers
sections.say: Does every sentence the reader sees say what the numbers behind it say?

checks.title: Every legend's numbers are its table's
checks.how: Each number in each figure legend was found in the statistics table the figure is drawn from.
checks.result: 43 of 43 legends checked; every number found.

checks.title: The methods name the right correction family
checks.how: The methods text's family size was compared with the number of models the code corrects across.
checks.result: The methods say the power contrasts are corrected across five regions; the code corrects across ten models (five regions, two bands).
detail: Either sentence or code must change; the numbers on the site use ten.

checks.title: Figure G1 reads as a lead it does not show
checks.how: The direction in each Granger figure's legend was compared with the two directions' Late to Early ratios.
checks.result: In Figure G1 both directions rise (1.42 and 1.37 times); the legend should say the coupling grew both ways, not that one region leads.

sections.title: It can be made again from the raw data
sections.say: Given the raw recordings and this code, would the same numbers come out?

checks.title: One rat worked out again from its raw recordings
checks.how: J6's Precon1 and Precon4 were read from the raw files and taken through tab 11 again in a separate folder.
checks.result: 20 of 20 values identical to the saved results.

checks.title: One file changed since the last commit
checks.how: git status was read for the files that make the results.
checks.result: backend/finalstage.py differs from the commit; commit it so the run can be named by its commit alone.

checks.title: Shuffles use a fixed seed
checks.how: The seed was read from each result file and the shuffle repeated once.
checks.result: Seed 20261030 everywhere; the repeated shuffle gave the same null.

sections.title: What a careful reader should know
sections.say: Nothing here is wrong, but each is worth reading before a result is believed.

checks.title: Eight rats is a small sample for a GEE
checks.how: Each result that passes was fitted again in a linear mixed model with Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.
checks.result: 4 of 6 GEE results do not pass in the mixed model; read them as leads.

checks.title: Pairs with PER or RSC have fewer rats
checks.how: Rats with a usable wire in both regions were counted for every pair.
checks.result: PER pairs have 5 or 6 rats and RSC pairs 7; a GEE with that few can read stronger than it is.
